requiredFindings.title: The presence marker ACE restricts the owner
requiredFindings.detail: group:<file gid> deny delete binds every member of the file's group, including the owner when the owner belongs to it (the default under a home directory or /var/folders/.../T). Measured under a primary-group parent: owner unlink, atomic rename-over, rename-away, rmdir and directory rename all fail with EACCES until chmod -N. The unit's own new test leaked two marked scratch directories in the owner's default TMPDIR at 15:12 because Scratch::drop's remove_dir_all was denied.
requiredFindings.fix: Use a behaviour-neutral marker. Measured: a zero-rights allow for the owner (tag 1, mask 0) captures as Entries(1) kind 1 rights 0 and leaves owner rename-over/unlink working; private_access accepts PERMIT with zero rights. user:nobody deny delete also works. Prefer the zero-rights allow.

requiredFindings.title: Whole-ACL replacement is an ACL policy action, not a presence marker, and can widen effective access
requiredFindings.detail: acl_set_fd_np(ACL_TYPE_EXTENDED) with a one-entry ACL discards all existing ACEs: explicit allow and deny (case C) and inherited foreign allows (case D). With no mode/owner precondition, discarding a deny can widen access: on a 0644 file with group:everyone deny read, the marker removes the deny and the mode bits again grant group/other read (case E). This contradicts 'presence marker', 'not creator policy' and 'does not grant access'.
requiredFindings.fix: Append the marker to the descriptor's existing ACL on the same fd (read, add entry, write back) so existing and inherited ACEs remain visible to capture and the predicate. Clearing inherited ACEs, if wanted, is creator policy for a separately reviewed unit with explicit preconditions (fresh object created in this operation, exact private mode, invoking-user owner).

requiredFindings.title: Production helpers without a production caller add 10 dead_code warnings and widen the unsafe production surface
requiredFindings.detail: install_non_granting_presence_ace and install_single_ace are production pub(crate) with no non-test caller; the platform lib build now reports 10 warnings (the two functions and eight FFI declarations). The workspace check was warning-free at every accepted state 447-450. The generic writer (any tag/mask/principal, including allows) moved from test-only to production.
requiredFindings.fix: Keep install_single_ace private to macos.rs; land the marker with its reviewed caller or keep it cfg(test) until the creator unit wires it; do not add allow(dead_code).

answerToQuestion: Replacing the whole ACL with one group deny of delete is NOT an acceptable presence marker: the deny locks the owner out of delete/rename when the owner is in the file's group (RF-1), and the replacement itself discards existing and inherited ACEs and can widen effective access (RF-2). Both are required findings.
